<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Determination of Fair Values </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In accordance with ASC 820-10-35, fair values are based on the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The following describes the assumptions and methodologies used to estimate the fair value of financial instruments recorded at fair value in the consolidated balance sheets and for estimating the fair value of financial instruments for which fair value is disclosed under ASC 825-10-50. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Investment Securities<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;When quoted prices are available in an active market, securities are classified as Level 1. For securities reported at fair value utilizing Level 2 inputs, the Company obtains fair value measurements from an independent pricing service. These fair value measurements consider observable market data that may include benchmark yield curves, reported trades, broker/dealer quotes, issuer spreads and credit information, among other inputs. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans Held for Sale<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;Loans held for sale are recorded at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value. Fair value is generally based on quoted market prices of similar loans and is considered to be Level 2. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net Loans<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;Loans are valued on an individual basis, with consideration given to the loans&#8217; underlying characteristics, including account types, remaining terms, annual interest rates or coupons, interest types, accrual basis, timing of principal and interest payments, current market rates, and remaining balances. A discounted cash flow model is used to estimate the fair value of the loans using assumptions for prepayments speeds, projected default probabilities by risk grade, and estimates of prevailing discount rates. The discounted cash flow approach models the projected cash flows, applying various assumptions regarding interest and payment risks for the loans based on the loan types, payment types and fixed or variable interest rate classifications. Estimated fair values are disclosed through the application of the exit price notion. The assumptions used to estimate fair value are intended to approximate those that a market participant would use in an orderly transaction on the measurement date.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivative Financial Instruments<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;Derivative financial instruments are measured at fair value based on modeling that utilizes observable market inputs for various interest rates published by leading third-party financial news and data providers. This is observable data that represents the rates used by market participants for instruments entered into at that date&#59; however, they are not based on actual transactions, so they are classified as Level 2. </span></p>
</ix:continuation><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">161</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_9a0be764-f785-428b-86a9-bca53cf83314" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_1d1dec0c-83ca-4015-b0f2-b8fde1887922">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deposits</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;The fair values disclosed for demand deposits are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (that is, their carrying amounts). Fair values for </span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">time deposits</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> are estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that </span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">uses recent issuance rates over the prior three months and a market rate analysis of recent offering rates for retail products</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> For wholesale products, brokered pricing offering rates were used.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">FHLB<span style="font-size:12pt;"> </span>Advances<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;The fair value of the FHLB advance approximates its book value.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Security Sold Under Agreements to Repurchase<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;The carrying amount of security repurchase agreements approximates their fair values. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Senior Debt<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;The fair value of senior debt was estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that uses recent issuance rates for similar debt offerings for similar sized issuers. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subordinated Debt.<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#160;The fair value of subordinated debentures was estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that uses recent issuance rates for similar debt offerings for similar sized issuers. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Junior Subordinated Debentures.<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#160;The fair value of junior subordinated debentures was estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that uses recent issuance rates for similar debt offerings for similar sized issuers. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes Payable.<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> The carrying amount of notes payable approximates the fair value.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Limitations<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.&#160;The following fair value estimates are determined as of a specific point in time utilizing various assumptions and estimates. The use of assumptions and various valuation techniques, as well as the absence of secondary markets for certain financial instruments, will likely reduce the comparability of fair value disclosures between financial institutions. The fair values for loans involve the use of various assumptions due to market-illiquidity as of December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018. These assumptions are considered to reflect inputs that market participants would use in transactions involving these instruments as of the measurement date. This table only includes financial instruments of the Company, and, accordingly, the total of the fair value amounts does not represent, and should not be construed to represent, the underlying value of the Company.</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000569" name="us-gaap:FairValueByBalanceSheetGroupingTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001614184_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000569_dcnt_101c7cac-8ee1-481b-be30-0bf11438483e">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000475" name="cade:VariableInterestEntitiesAndOtherInvestmentsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001614184_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000475_dcnt_c5d09acf-c93a-42f8-8f0f-adeacd07e2c2">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 21&#8212;Variable Interest Entities and Other Investments</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under ASC 810-10-65, the Company is deemed to be the primary beneficiary and required to consolidate a variable interest entity (&#8220;VIE&#8221;) if it has a variable interest in the VIE that provides it with a controlling financial interest. For such purposes, the determination of whether a controlling financial interest exists is based on whether a single party has both the power to direct the activities of the VIE that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance and the obligation to absorb the losses of the VIE or the right to receive benefits from the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE. ASC 810-10-65, as amended, requires continual reconsideration of conclusions reached regarding which interest holder is a VIE&#8217;s primary beneficiary.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Bank has invested in several affordable housing projects as a limited partner. The partnerships have qualified to receive annual affordable housing federal tax credits that are recognized as a reduction of current tax expense. The Company has determined that these structures meet the definition of VIE&#8217;s under ASC 810 but that consolidation is not required, as the Bank is not the primary beneficiary. At December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, the Bank&#8217;s maximum exposure to loss associated with these limited partnerships was limited to the Bank&#8217;s investment. The Company accounts for these investments and the related tax credits using either the effective yield method or the proportional amortization method, depending upon the date of the investment. Under the effective yield method, the Bank recognizes the tax credits as they are allocated and amortizes the initial costs of the investments to provide a constant effective yield over the period that the tax credits are allocated. Under the proportional amortization method, the Bank amortizes the cost of the investment in proportion to the tax credits and other tax benefits received and recognizes the net investment performance in the income statement as a component of income tax expense. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cadence&#8217;s investment in certain marketable equity securities are carried at fair value and are reported in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. Total marketable equity securities were $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002594" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNi" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002595" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNi" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">5.8</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2016, the Bank received net profits interests in oil and gas reserves, in connection with the reorganization under bankruptcy of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_cadeCustomer" id="F_002596" name="cade:NumberOfLoanCustomers" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20161231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> loan customers (<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_cadeCustomer" id="F_002597" name="cade:NumberOfLoanCustomersSold" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> of these was sold during 2018). The Company has determined that these contracts meet the definition of VIE&#8217;s under Topic ASC 810, but that consolidation is not required as the Bank is not the primary beneficiary. The net profits interests are financial instruments and recorded at estimated fair value, which was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002598" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityEntityMaximumLossExposureAmount" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="6">4.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002599" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityEntityMaximumLossExposureAmount" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="6">5.8</ix:nonFraction> million at December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, respectively, representing the maximum exposure to loss as of that date.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has established a rabbi trust related to the deferred compensation plan offered to certain of its employees. The Company contributes employee cash compensation deferrals to the trust. The assets of the trust are available to creditors of the Company only in the event the Company becomes insolvent. This trust is considered a VIE because either there is no equity at risk in the trust or because the Company provided the equity interest to its employees in exchange for services rendered. The Company is considered the primary beneficiary of the rabbi trust as it has the ability to select the underlying investments made by the trust, the activities that most significantly impact the economic performance of the rabbi trust. The Company includes the assets of the rabbi trust as a component of other assets and a corresponding liability for the associated benefit obligation in other liabilities in its consolidated balance sheets. The amount of rabbi trust assets and benefit obligation was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002600" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligation" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_cadeRabbiTrustMember_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">3.7</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002601" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligation" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_cadeRabbiTrustMember_us-gaapVariableInterestEntitiesByClassificationOfEntityAxis_us-gaapVariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">3.6</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000476" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001614184_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000476_dcnt_58a492d9-8f84-4a48-bfee-ad0bde0d40ed">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 22&#8212;Segment Reporting<span style="color:#2E74B5;font-weight:normal;"> </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company determines reportable segments based on the services offered, the significance of the services offered, the significance of those services to the Company&#8217;s financial condition and operating results and management&#8217;s regular review of the operating results of those services. The Company operates through <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_cadeSegment" id="F_002602" name="us-gaap:NumberOfOperatingSegments" contextRef="C_0001614184_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction> operating segments: Banking, Financial Services and Corporate. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Banking Segment includes the Commercial Banking, Retail Banking and Private Banking lines of business. The Commercial Banking line of business includes a general business services component primarily focusing on commercial&#160;&#38; industrial (C&#38;I), community banking, business banking and commercial real estate lending to clients in the geographic footprint in Texas and the southeast United States. In addition, the Commercial Banking line of business includes within C&#38;I a separate component that focuses on select industries (which is referred to as the &#8220;specialized industries&#8221;) in which the Company believes it has specialized experience and service capabilities, including energy, healthcare, restaurant industry, and technology. The </p>
</ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">164</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000476_dcnt_58a492d9-8f84-4a48-bfee-ad0bde0d40ed">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Company serve</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">s</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> clients in these specialized industries both within the geographic footprint and throughout the United States as a result of the national orientation of many of these businesses. The Retail Banking line of business offers a broad range of retail banking services including mortgage services through the branch network to serve the needs of consumer and small businesses in the geographic footprint. The Private Banking line of business offers banking services and loan products tailored to the needs of the high-net worth clients in the geographic footprint.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Financial Services Segment includes the Trust, Retail Brokerage, and Investment Services lines of business. These businesses offer products independently to their own customers as well as to Banking Segment clients. Investment Services operates through the &#8220;Linscomb&#160;&#38; Williams&#8221; name. The products offered by the businesses in the Financial Services Segment primarily generate non-banking service fee income. The Corporate Segment reflects parent-only activities and intercompany eliminations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Business segment results are determined based upon the management reporting system, which assigns balance sheet and income statement items to each of the business segments. The process is designed around the organizational and management structure and, accordingly, the results derived are not necessarily comparable with similar information published by other financial institutions or in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company evaluates performance and allocates resources based on profit or loss from operations. There are no material inter-segment sales or transfers. The accounting policies used by each reportable segment are the same as those discussed in Note 1. All costs, except corporate administration and income taxes, have been allocated to the reportable segments. Therefore, combined amounts agree to the consolidated totals.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000572" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001614184_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 23&#8212;Equity-based Compensation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company administers a long-term incentive compensation plan that permits the granting of incentive awards in the form of stock options, restricted stock, restricted stock units, performance units, stock appreciation rights, or other stock-based awards. The terms of all awards issued under these plans are determined by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Amended and Restated 2015 Omnibus Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;) permits the Company to grant to employees and directors various forms of incentive compensation. The principal purposes of this plan are to focus directors, officers, and other employees and consultants on business performance that creates shareholder value, to encourage innovative approaches to the business of the Company, and to encourage ownership of the Company&#8217;s stock. The Plan authorizes <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_002681" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_cadeTwoZeroOneFiveOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="6">7.5</ix:nonFraction> million common share equivalents available for grant, where grants of full value awards (e.g., shares of restricted stock, restricted stock units and performance stock units) count as one share equivalent. The number of remaining share equivalents available for future issuance under the Plan was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_002682" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001614184_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_cadeTwoZeroOneFiveOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="6">4.1</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2019.</p>

For the performance-based restricted stock units granted, these performance conditions will determine the actual units vesting and can be in the range of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002728" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001614184_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_cadeTwoZeroOneFiveOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_us-gaapVestingAxis_us-gaapShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2">25</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002729" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001614184_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_cadeTwoZeroOneFiveOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_us-gaapVestingAxis_us-gaapShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2">200</ix:nonFraction>% of the units granted.&#160;These grants include rights as a shareholder in the form of dividend equivalents. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures:<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:Calibri;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </span><span style="color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">As of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K, our management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have evaluated our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)). Based upon that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective in ensuring that information required to be disclosed is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Commission&#8217;s rules and forms and are also designed to ensure that the information required to be disclosed in the reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosures.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management's Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">. The Report of Management on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and the attestation report on our internal control over financial reporting issued by Ernst &#38; Young LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm that audited our consolidated financial statements, are included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.65%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> No change in our internal control over financial reporting occurred during the fourth fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2019 covered by this Annual Report that materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</span></p>
